angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 178,682,892 km at 343.64 pc = 6.95 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 33856: distance 343.643 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.065), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 343.643 +/- 22.337 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 2.5085 +/- 0.1590 mas (same row, RUWE 2.55), 15.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 256.839 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 33856: radius 256.839 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 12254.2 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.093) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 178,682,892 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3792 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 33856: effective temperature 3792 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.06) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 33856: effective temperature 3792 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.06) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * sig CMa: spectral type K5Ib (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * sig CMa: main object type s*r, Red Supergiant

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.05 from 2007A&A...475.1003H; the 3 published values span log g 1 to 1.05, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007A%26A...475.1003H)
